hosted.summary: Hosted arm, on DEV: judge v1 paid more often than the companies did for 2 of 2 models; across the 2 models and both prompts, 4 of 4 comparisons with the issuer lookup were below it, 0 were above it and the rest were not distinguishable (claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5). The design compares each model with the issuer lookup and with the record, not models with one another; it does not show that the results are independent of the model. Reference rows, descriptive only: claude-opus-5-5 (reasoning on, cannot be disabled; 4096 max_tokens; not part of the comparisons; complete). claude-opus-5-5 ran with adaptive thinking, which it does not allow to be turned off, at effort low and max_tokens 4096. Its thinking tokens are given per cell in the table. It is a reference row, not part of the comparisons. claude-haiku-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 ran without up-front thinking and max_tokens 512, as the local models did. The one person who labelled the sample agreed with the record at kappa 0.202 [-0.054, 0.456] on his 56 decided labels, so neither the record nor this person is a gold standard. Each model's closeness to the record and to this person is given with its interval; the models are not ranked, and no model is called the best. Same vendor. The three models under test are Anthropic's. So is the AI coding assistant that wrote this repository, drafted both judge prompts, proposed these three models and their settings, and wrote this amendment and this arm's code; the model behind the earlier drafting of the prompts is not recorded here. The agent that wrote this arm's code ran on `claude-opus-5-5`, one of the three models evaluated here, and so did every independent review of this amendment; the coordinating assistant ran on `claude-fable-5-2`. The translation the annotator read beside each labelled complaint was made by `claude-fable-5-2`, also Anthropic's, though not one of the three. This amendment is published, and the hosted run starts, only after all seven local models are closed. This arm does not measure whether any of this favours the vendor's models. Cost: claude-haiku-5-5 0.12 USD (600 answers, 0 charged without an answer; 964520 input, 40400 output and 0 thinking tokens); claude-sonnet-5-5 2.32 USD (600 answers, 0 charged without an answer; 964520 input, 39279 output and 0 thinking tokens); claude-opus-5-5 4.61 USD (600 answers, 0 charged without an answer; 965120 input, 37640 output and 78 thinking tokens); 7.05 USD in all, under a cap of 15 USD. No request was resent or charged without an answer.

post_run_changes.what: third change, after the held-out run: the venv target checks the Python version (the pinned numpy and scipy need 3.12 or later) and stops with a message before pip runs; PYTHON names the interpreter. No other line changed. Sixth change, after the held-out run and the human labels: a `sql` target that runs python -m judge.sql (load the data into SQLite in memory, run every query in sql/, print the results). No other line changed. Ninth change, before any request of the local-models extension: a `models` target that runs one model of that extension, and `check` also runs `python -m judge.models --verify`. Tenth change, before any request of the hosted arm: a `models-hosted` target that runs one model of that arm (the key is read from the environment when a request is sent and named nowhere in the target), and `check` also runs `python -m judge.hosted --verify`.

added after the held-out run and after the blind labels were locked (eighth change): the plan for running judge v1 and v2, with the frozen prompts and options, on four other local models (qwen3.5:9b, gemma4:12b, phi4:14b, mistral-small3.2:24b) on DEV and the labelled sample only, written by the AI coding assistant at the author's request and committed before any of those models was sent a complaint. Not run; computes nothing and feeds no reported number. Ninth change: Amendment 1 appended below the registered text, which is unchanged (lines 1-149 equal 162909f): labels instead of verdicts, the summary sentence fixed in advance, neutral sampling penalties in every request, refusal and interruption rules with no replacement, publication before the first request, malformed answers read three ways, the Ollama version and updates, the fixed order and first-screen sentence, what will not be concluded, the checks, three more models (granite4.1:30b, glm-4.7-flash:latest, gemma4:31b) and a hosted arm left to a possible Amendment 2. Not run. Tenth change: Amendment 2 appended below Amendment 1, which is unchanged, as are lines 1-149: a separately registered hosted arm on three models of one vendor (claude-haiku-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 compared, without reasoning; claude-opus-5-5, whose reasoning cannot be switched off, a descriptive reference row under the plan's exclusion rule) on DEV and the labelled sample only, with the exact request and the documentation each choice was checked on, the differences from the local runs, a 15 USD cap enforced in code and never raised, the interruption and retry rules (no model is ever dropped), its own table, corrected levels, summary sentence and README section with no ranking, the same-vendor disclosure, the order of events, and publication before the first request; it notes that Amendment 1, section 13, foresaw an open-weights hosted arm instead. Revised after four independent reviews before publication. Not run.

added after the held-out run: the deviations list moved out of the README, with the second post-run change added. Third change: the third post-run change recorded, the four freezes named, the wording of AI-agent reviews and of frozen files, and the labelling-aid entry rewritten without grading the annotator. Fourth change: the fourth post-run change recorded, including that commit 7194269 was made with four failing tests and why; the registered v3 step recorded as not carried out. Fifth change: the fifth post-run change recorded, including the removal of three unused personal-data columns from data/live_api_metadata.csv.gz and why; the v3 entry says that the plan anticipated the small halves. Sixth change: the sixth post-run change recorded (the baselines in SQL, and wording corrections to the version published at 72b077a); the fifth-change entry marks the person's kappa on each half as registered. Seventh change: the seventh post-run change recorded (a clause about the author's own level removed from the introduction of docs/sql.md, with no change to who is stated to have written the SQL; links made clickable); the same clause removed from the sixth-change entry. Eighth change: the eighth post-run change recorded (a plan to run the same task on four other local models, registered before any of them was sent a complaint; not run). Ninth change: the ninth post-run change recorded (Amendment 1 of the local-models plan, three more models, the runner and analysis code and the public record, before any request). Tenth change: the tenth post-run change recorded (Amendment 2 of the local-models plan, a hosted arm, and its code, before any request to it; not run). Eleventh change: the eleventh post-run change recorded (the results of the model extension, both arms, with the run facts, what was computed, where the registered code does not produce what the plan promises, and what was added after the results were seen; after two reviews, completed: the registered outputs computed after the results were seen, the corrected wording and the correction of two statements of the first version; after a gate review, which reviews re-derived what, and where the re-derivation test takes TF-IDF's decisions).

added after the held-out run and after the blind labels were locked (sixth change): a plain-English walk-through of every query in sql/, clause by clause, written by the AI coding assistant; it explains every query clause by clause for a reader new to SQL; it says which printed figures were already reported and which are printed for the first time (descriptive), and what a run on PostgreSQL 14 showed; its expected outputs are written by python -m judge.sql --docs and checked by a snapshot test. Computes nothing. Seventh change (at the author's decision): a clause about the author's own level was removed from the introduction; it still says that the AI coding assistant that wrote the rest of the code chose and wrote the queries, the loader, the tests and the walk-through, after the held-out run and the human labels, because a review by a separate AI-agent session asked what the SQL for the issuer-rate baseline and the same-issuer pairs would be and the author then asked for an SQL section, and that the walk-through explains every query clause by clause for a reader new to SQL. This record's sixth-change text was edited the same way. Computes nothing.

added after the held-out run, after the blind labels were locked and after both arms of the model extension had run (eleventh change, after two reviews); written after the results were seen. Computes the registered outputs of the extension that the registered analysis code leaves out, with the plan's definitions unchanged (docs/analysis_plan_models.md, lines 81-95): accuracy against the record and against the person under both registered readings (metrics.bootstrap), judge minus TF-IDF on DEV (metrics.paired_difference against the study's TF-IDF model with its frozen settings), and the payout share minus the record's with its paired interval for every cell (models_analysis.paired). No label. Feeds no frozen number.

added after the held-out run, after the blind labels were locked and after both arms of the model extension had run (eleventh change): the README sections and full-report sections of the extension (docs/analysis_plan_models.md, Amendments 1 and 2). It runs models_analysis.analyse and hosted_analysis.analyse unchanged and prints their output, the arms' run records from their journals and run logs, the registered summary sentences word for word, the intervals and corrected-level words the registered code computes but does not print, the one first-screen sentence per amendment, a list of the registered outputs the code does not produce, and a short note headed 'Exploratory (not registered)' with descriptive payout counts.
